title: Can Senolytics Help Reverse Aging?
abstract:
### **The Rise of**Senolytics  
Once relegated to the outer rings of biohacker fantasy, senolytics—an evolving suite of compounds, supplements, and in-office therapies aimed at purging the body of its most indolent cells—are now edging into the mainstream as a promising way to delay the cellular entropy we’ve come to call aging.  
In 2024, [the global market for senolytics](https://www.precedenceresearch.com/senolytics-and-anti-aging-pharmaceuticals-market) and anti-aging drugs was valued at over $4 billion, with the wellness and longevity segment accounting for $1.69 billion of that total. And the research is catching up: [more than 30 clinical trials](https://clinicaltrials.gov/search?term=senolytic) are currently underway or completed, testing compounds like [dasatinib, quercetin](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36637079/), and [fisetin](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30279143/) for everything from lung disease to Alzheimer’s to premature aging in cancer survivors.
### **Developing a Senolytics Protocol: What You Need to Know**  
The longevity conversation isn’t limited to injections or peptide therapy. “Important senolytics I use in my practice include quercetin and urolithin A,” says Kahn. Both compounds are available in supplement form and have anti-inflammatory and mitochondrial-supporting properties. “Quercetin has anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-viral properties, while Urolithin A is made naturally by gut bacteria and supports mitochondrial health and the healthy removal of damaged mitochondria, which protects against senescent cell formation and accumulation.”  
But how much of this can you do yourselves? “There’s a wide spectrum — from over-the-counter serums and antioxidant-rich skincare to prescription biologics and in-office regenerative therapies. The key is to do your homework,” says Wyles.
“One way to help clear out senescent cells, according to Kahn, is by triggering autophagy—a natural process in which the body breaks down and recycles damaged or dysfunctional cells. This cellular hoovering can be stimulated through [intermittent fasting](https://goop.com/wellness/health/intermittent-fasting-evidence/?srsltid=AfmBOoqkzjQYEymnvwJ1JDe3LipLTnW2Huy7a2VcuUolWMniezUwju7c), [regular exercise](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37582398/), [mTOR inhibition](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36014530/), and [hyperbaric oxygen therapy](https://goop.com/wellness/health/hyperbaric-oxygen-therapy-benefits-and-risks/?srsltid=AfmBOoopu_gNCTNocPcKhNbzg7YQXovbUF5BCN70TFxHodzi15ElJoBx). Regenerative therapies like [red light](https://goop.com/wellness/health/does-red-light-therapy-work/?srsltid=AfmBOopznZL4n0zVcy-eeDRrRhQTWFcvPnt2ZGVIScrxZpwQLDNgcSW0) and [cold plunging](https://goop.com/breathwork-and-the-wim-hof-method/?srsltid=AfmBOoqNvU-n6B2aGrFHtW2QMcDPH5-0Pz7C6MY0abG2xztiD5o9P7RE) may also support this process when paired with personalized medical guidance.” Keep in mind: Any senolytic protocol has to be highly personalized to your body, your family history, and your goals. Be sure to consult your doctor to customize a treatment plan for you and to monitor your progress.
